[[File:Cavalier Hotel Virginia Beach postcard.jpg|thumb|right|260px|The Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach.]]
[[File:Cavalier Hotel Virginia Beach 2019.jpg|thumb|right|260px|The Cavalier Hotel, 2019. Photo: Carol M. Highsmith.]]
'''1999 Decipher World Championship''' was the fourth Star Wars CCG World Championship, played 12–13 November 1999 at [[DecipherCon 1999]] in the Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia. [[Gary Carman]] (United Kingdom) defeated [[Steven Lewis]] (United States) 2 (+19) and became the first British World Champion.<ref name="trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]]</ref><ref name="sw">[https://web.archive.org/web/19991128144348/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/index.html Star Wars CCG World Championship], Decipher (Wayback 28 November 1999)</ref><ref name="sat">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001120012500/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/saturday.html Lalumiere Saturday], DecipherCon '99 (Wayback 20 November 2000)</ref>

The site was the same Cavalier Hotel that hosted the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]]. [[Kendrick Summers]] announced DecipherCon for the Cavalier Resort and Hotel in Virginia Beach on 27 September 1999.<ref name="rfd26">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrkKhWcstAs Broadcast 26 - Radio Free Decipher], Kendrick Summers (27 September 1999). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-OrkKhWcstAs Internet Archive]. Watch page: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010122343/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrkKhWcstAs Internet Archive].</ref>

The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Endor]]. [[Enhanced Cloud City]] was not legal in the World Championship decks. Decipher sold that product from 9am Saturday for other convention events, including the Invitational and the Sunday Team Challenge.<ref name="ecc">[https://web.archive.org/web/19991128112134/http://www.decipher.com/newsflash/1999/1099/102699storyA.html Star Wars CCG Enhanced Cloud City and the '99 World Championships], Kendrick Summers, Decipher (26 October 1999)</ref>

Thursday 11 November 1999 was the Wild Card, an open tournament at [[DecipherCon 1999]]. The top two advanced to Friday Day 1 of the World Championship. [[John Arendt]] finished first and [[James Lafferty]] finished second.<ref name="rfd112" /><ref name="lafferty-dd" /><ref name="trando" /> Both played Day 1. Lafferty played all three days. [[Matt Sokol]] placed 3rd.<ref name="iv16">[http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Internet Archive]</ref> [[Francis Lalumiere]] counted 146 Star Wars players in that event.<ref name="thu">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000903021929/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/thursday.html Lalumiere Thursday], DecipherCon '99 (Wayback 3 September 2000)</ref> Qualification was more exclusive than 1997–1998: one player per region plus Open, Wild Card, and invitational seats. The regional structure drew heavy criticism and was not kept for 2000. [[Joe Alread]] won Ironman and missed the main event for the first time.<ref name="trando" />

Day 1 (32 players, eight games): [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] led on 13 (143), then [[Clint Hays]] on 13 (80). Carman finished third on 12 (71) after a strong close. [[Matt Lush]] finished 28th. That evening Carman lost his decks and rebuilt overnight, borrowing and adjusting Markus Wuest's Light.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="final12">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000122170128/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/final12.html They advanced to the Round of 12], Decipher (Wayback 22 January 2000)</ref><ref name="lush">Matt Lush, [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/1999-11-16-day-one-world-championshipsd110/ day-one-world-championships], DeckTech (16 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009094534/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/1999-11-16-day-one-world-championshipsd110/ Internet Archive]</ref>

Day 2 (four games): [[Yannick Lapointe]] was the early leader; Winkelhaus and Hays took early losses. Lewis was the only undefeated and met Carman in the Final Confrontation.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="sw03" />

== Format ==

* '''Environment:''' [[Premiere - Endor]] ([[Enhanced Cloud City]] excluded)<ref name="ecc" />
* '''Site:''' [[DecipherCon 1999]], Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia
* '''Dates:''' Wild Card Thursday 11 November 1999. Worlds Day 1 Friday 12 November 1999; Day 2 and Final Confrontation Saturday 13 November. The convention ran 11–14 November.
* '''Field:''' 32 (4 Open + 2 Invitational + 23 Regional + 2 Wild Card + 1 defending).<ref name="field">[https://web.archive.org/web/19991128125001/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/finalists.html Finalists], Decipher (Wayback 28 November 1999)</ref>

== Wild Card ==

Thursday 11 November 1999 was an open constructed event at DecipherCon. The top two advanced to Friday Day 1 of the World Championship.<ref name="field" /><ref name="thu" /><ref name="trando" />

Francis K. Lalumiere wrote at 9:10 p.m. that 146 Star Wars players were in that event. Worlds started on Friday.<ref name="thu" /> Decipher's score sheet lists 147 players.<ref name="dc99sw01_1">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW01_1.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: 1999 SW Wildcard], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011101231420/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW01_1.html Internet Archive]</ref> Play ran into Friday morning. Decipher wrote that [[James Lafferty]]'s 2nd place was not secured until 1 a.m. Friday.<ref name="lafferty-dd">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000301030330/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/deckdesigns/121099laffertylight.html James Lafferty Light], Decipher Deck Designs (Wayback 1 March 2000)</ref>

[[John Arendt]] finished first.<ref name="rfd112">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=docK2vpQWUI&t=880s Broadcast 112 - Radio Free Decipher], Scott Gaeta (25 January 2002), at 14:40. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-docK2vpQWUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 112 transcript]].</ref> [[James Lafferty]] finished second.<ref name="lafferty-dd" /> Those two played Day 1 on Friday. [[Matt Sokol]] placed 3rd; only the top 2 advanced.<ref name="iv16" /> [[Scott Lingrell]] posted an 8–2 record in the Wild Card. [[Christopher Kagehiro]] and [[Stephanie Kagehiro]] played a Game 2 match. [[Kim Caton]] of Philadelphia won Wild Card Game 2.<ref name="lingrell-wc">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/1354 Yavin IVCheese], DeckTech (Scott "CRingwell" Lingrell, 22 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261024191350/https://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/1354/ Internet Archive]</ref>

== Final Confrontation ==

The match was Saturday after Day 2. Lewis was the only undefeated in the round of 12 and met Carman.<ref name="sw03" /><ref name="trando" /> [[Kathy Lischke]] announced the two finalists on Decipher's event board.<ref name="kl-final">[http://calder.decipher.com/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$7077-13141$1 "Star Wars: CCG Final Confrontation"], [[Kathy Lischke]], DecipherCon: Event Report Board, Decipher (13 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001025033142/http://calder.decipher.com:80/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$7077-13141$1 Internet Archive]</ref>

Game 1: Carman [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] (Outer Rim Scout) against Lewis's Clak'dor VII Operative Speeder ([[Local Uprising / Liberation|Local Uprising]]). Carman won by 22.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="tfn">[http://www.theforce.net/videogames/story/CCG_World_Champion_78174.asp CCG World Champion], TheForce.Net (14 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20160101143010/http://www.theforce.net/videogames/story/CCG_World_Champion_78174.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

Game 2: Carman [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]] inserts against Lewis [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down]]. Lewis probed the Hidden Base with Security Precautions. Carman resolved Never Tell Me The Odds for 8 after Grimtaash stripped Torture. Lewis won by 3 with Lateral Damage. Combined, Carman 2 (+19).<ref name="trando" /><ref name="tfn" />

[[Mark Tuttle]] called game 2 the most exciting match he had ever watched. Decipher posted his play-by-play audio of both games.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="sw" /> Francis K. Lalumiere called Carman's win the last World Champion title of the millennium.<ref name="sat" />

Carman's published lists are the rebuilt pair from Friday night. He had lost the decks he used on Day 1.<ref name="trando" /> Lischke's same-day report said he found the decks missing on Saturday morning. He built two new decks with help from another qualifier and had never played them before the final.<ref name="kl-necessity">[http://calder.decipher.com/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$10751-27562$1 "Necessity is the mother of invention"], [[Kathy Lischke]], DecipherCon: Event Report Board, Decipher (13 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001028020703/http://calder.decipher.com:80/cgi-bin/msgbd?dconerb$10751-27562$1 Internet Archive]</ref>

== Tournament reports ==

Players' own reports from this event.

* [[Martin Akesson World Championships by Martin Akesson (tournament report)]] — by [[Martin Akesson]], 7th, 7–5

''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' writer [[Richard Handley]] covered the event in "[[All Decked Out (Star Wars Insider)|All Decked Out]]" for issue 48, with quotes from Carman, Lewis and the top 12 list. He also took the article's photographs.<ref name="swi48">Rich Handley, "All Decked Out", ''Star Wars Insider'' 48 (2000), pp. 78–79; listed in the contents as "Decipher This!". Scan: [https://archive.org/details/star-wars-insider-56b702/page/n81/mode/2up Internet Archive].</ref>

== Discrepancies ==

Where a source disagrees with the record on the article, the article keeps the record and notes the difference here.

* Akesson writes that he placed 7th on Day 1 with 10 (+46); Decipher's round-of-12 list has him 8th on 10 (45), behind James Lafferty on the same score.<ref name="tr-d163">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-01-09-world-championships-by-martin-akessond163/ world-championships-by-martin-akesson], DeckTech (Martin "Mart" Akesson, 9 January 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261025134508/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-01-09-world-championships-by-martin-akessond163/ Internet Archive]</ref>
* Akesson's game scores give a Day 2 total of 4 (−12); Decipher's SW.03 Day 2 scores have him on 4 (−9).<ref name="tr-d163" />
* Lischke's 13 November board report places Carman's deck rebuild on Saturday morning; the Trandosite interview places it on Friday night.<ref name="kl-necessity" /><ref name="trando" />
